26	## §0 Why taxonomy is the curation gate
27	
28	Every research entity downstream of this document — slugs, search-log entries, BPC
29	files, evidence rows, item links — inherits its selection and attachment rules from
30	the taxonomy. A source is only findable if some entity names what it is evidence
31	*about*; it is only curatable if an entity exists for it to attach *to*.
32	
33	Axes are framed as **person-environment interaction dimensions** — where a person's
34	functioning meets an environmental demand — per armature §5 ("Axes are framed as
35	person-environment interaction dimensions where possible") and the mission's
36	biopsychosocial ground. The taxonomy names demands the *environment* places on
37	variable bodies, which is the part designers control; it does not define bodies by
38	deficit. **[T1][T2]** Where an ICF `b`-code anchor (a body-function code) appears,
39	it serves *findability* — reaching the clinical literatures indexed that way — and
40	never serves as a description of any person (population-taxonomy §1.1: codes are
41	"an organizing convenience, not a definition of people").
42	
43	The 2026-07-21 audit found both curation failure modes live:
44	
45	- **Findability failure:** balance/vestibular function was named in canon
46	  (armature §5 lists a vestibular axis; `population-taxonomy.md` NEU/PCS names
47	  "vestibular") yet is **operationally invisible**: zero ICF b-codes corpus-wide,
48	  zero slugs, zero searches in any of 19 tracked languages. Conceptual presence
49	  without curation machinery produced structural absence. **Caveat [T1]:** the
50	  absence checks were run with English search terms over an EN-heavy corpus; the
51	  non-English validation gate (§9.2) exists precisely because "missing" so far
52	  means "missing-in-English."
53	- **Attachment failure:** evidence about MS thermal intolerance attaches to a
54	  diagnosis shelved under "neurological" — an etiological placement — so sibling
55	  populations with the same functional demand (SCI poikilothermia, POTS, older
56	  adults) cannot reach it.
57	
58	## §0.5 The irreducibility principle (governs everything below)
59	
60	This principle governs how every table, axis, and mapping in this document is to be
61	read. It is `held-tensions.md` T9 operationalized for the axis model, and it is
62	binding: no downstream use may read the taxonomy against it.
63	
64	1. **A spectrum along a spectrum.** Every axis is a continuum, and a person's
65	   position on it is itself contextual, fluctuating, and fuzzy — not a fixed
66	   coordinate. The register discretizes for retrieval; the discretization is a
67	   property of the *tool*, not of the person. `fluctuating: yes/no` is a coarse flag
68	   over a condition that is, in truth, universal: all function varies by the hour,
69	   the setting, and the meaning of the task.
70	
71	2. **Axes describe specifications, not persons.** Per armature §4.2, axes are "the
72	   dimensions along which built-environment *specifications* vary." They are a
73	   property of the specification space, not a decomposition of a human being.
74	   `population_axis_map` (§4) is therefore a **retrieval index and navigation
75	   hypothesis**, graded by mapping-confidence (§3.2) — **never a portrait**. A person
76	   is never the join of their axis values, and the taxonomy makes no claim that they
77	   are.
78	
79	3. **Measured function is not independent of selfhood.** The same axis value
80	   manifests differently by fatigue, familiarity, culture, mood, history, and the
81	   meaning the task holds for the person. This is not a caveat; it is the shared
82	   claim of three of the project's four declared frameworks — ICF's own
83	   *capacity vs. performance* gap (what a body can do in a standard room is not what
84	   this person does in their life), Kawa's inseparable flow of self-context-function,
85	   and the Capability Approach's conversion factors. No axis value is a stored
86	   attribute; each is provisional and context-relative.
87	
88	4. **The person is the ground truth; the specification serves them.** A specification
89	   is an approximation in service of an individual — a starting hypothesis for a
90	   conversation, never a verdict about them (mission #7). Person Mode is not the
91	   exception the model escalates to; it is the reality the model approximates
92	   (mission #4: the population range "neither bounds nor defines the person"). Every
93	   default is overridable at the individual value (armature §4.3).
94	
95	5. **The irreducible remainder has a home.** What no coordinate captures — why two
96	   people at identical axis values live different lives — is curated in the
97	   `situations` entity (§5.4) and in Co-1 testimony, which are never subordinated to
98	   axis-level evidence (§3.1). Their existence in the schema is the project's
99	   structural admission that the person exceeds the profile.
100	
101	**Consequence for the enterprise (stated honestly).** Pushed to its end, this
102	principle is in tension with the whole idea of a specification guide. The project's
103	answer is that a generalization held *as* a generalization, with the individual as
104	the override and the ground truth, raises the floor where no individual assessment is
105	available — which is most of the built world, most of the time. The taxonomy is
106	legitimate only as an approximation in service of the individual, never as a portrait
107	of them. Where it is read as a portrait, it is being misused.
108	
109	**Owner adjudication (2026-07-21).** The enterprise-legitimacy question this principle
110	raises is settled in favour of proceeding: *something is better than nothing, and a
111	solution that serves 95% beats one that serves 50%.* The generalization is legitimate
112	**as the floor**; the individual override (Person Mode, situations, Co-1) carries the
113	remainder, so shipping the floor is not conceding the tail. This closes the ratified
114	posture — the taxonomy generalizes openly and declares that it does; it does not wait
115	for a per-person completeness it can never reach.
116

Both positions are recorded; the owner adjudicates |

207	## §3 Layer 2 — Profiles
208	
209	A **profile** is who evidence is about: population codes (canonical Layer 2
210	identifiers), diagnosis-level, identity-level, demographic, anthropometric,
211	compound, and umbrella groupings — each carrying weighted axis mappings *plus
212	authored emergent content that is never derived from, and never reduced to, the
213	axis layer*.
214	
215	### §3.1 The emergence guarantee **[T3]**
216	
217	Mature design corpora — DeafSpace, dementia-friendly design, ASPECTSS, age-friendly
218	design, DBL tactile-first practice — are authored at profile level and are not
219	reconstructable from axis sums. Profile-level and Co-1 evidence curate against
220	profiles and are never subordinated: Co-1 is encoded `tier: 1` (mission #3), so
221	lived-experience evidence anchors full-strength (●) claims. Conflicts between
222	profile guidance and axis-derived guidance display at parity (held-tensions T7);
223	no precedence rule exists.
224	
225	### §3.2 Mapping confidence (adopted from armature §4.2) **[T2][T4]**
226	
227	Diagnosis-to-axis mappings are *navigation hypotheses, not prescriptions*, graded:
228	**high-predictive** (confident pre-fill; e.g. complete T6 SCI), **moderate**
229	(sub-classification prompt; validated scaffolds), **low** (explicit high-variation
230	disclosure; e.g. MS, ABI), **minimal** (no pre-fill; population content + direct
231	axis entry; e.g. IntD). Each mapping's confidence is itself a documented claim with
232	provenance. This replaces v1.0's flat PRIMARY/SECONDARY roles as the honesty
233	mechanism; the staged schema carries both (role for query weighting, confidence for
234	disclosure).
235	
236	### §3.3 Membership doctrine **[T2][T4]**
237	
238	**Diagnosis-optional.** Profiles describe; they never gate. Axis entry retrieves
239	every specification with no population selection (armature §4.3 — the two paths are
240	peers), so no diagnosis, certification, or code is ever a condition of any
241	provision, any Co-1 attachment, or any reader's use. **ICD-11 negative
242	commitment:** ICD anchors on diagnostic profiles serve interoperability and
243	disambiguation only; they are never required for membership, never gate content,
244	and are never used to rank populations. Identity profiles (Deaf community;
245	identity-model neurodivergence) carry **no** ICD anchor by design.
246	
247	**Naming.** Person-first vs identity-first conventions differ *between communities
248	and between languages*; the taxonomy defers to each community's stated preference
249	in English and to native-language conventions via `term_aliases` — display names
250	are presentation-layer, revisable without schema change **[T1][T5]**.
251	
252	**Work from axes — no armchair umbrellas [T2][T4][T9].** Curation, demand-mapping,
253	and specification proceed *from the axes* (Layer 1) — the specific, architect-
254	actionable, diagnosis-neutral, co-occurrence-native demand dimensions — **never from
255	broad population/profile umbrellas.** The profile layer is populated only with
256	*specific self-identified communities on their own terms* (co-produced); it is never
257	a place to coin lumped coalition codes from an armchair. Broad umbrellas (e.g.
258	"physically disabled", or clinical-cluster relabels like "energy-limiting chronic
259	illness") are **forbidden as profile codes** because they (a) collapse opposed and
260	orthogonal design demands and (b) erase specific communities — the exact
261	pre-taxonomy category-thinking §1.3 and §0.5 exist to end. A population is a
262	mapping-confidence-weighted **vector over axes** (§3.2), not a bucket. **The impulse
263	to reach for a population umbrella is the signal to STOP and decompose to axes
264	instead**; umbrellas may exist only as additive cross-cutting *tags* over specifics,
265	never as replacement codes. Provenance and the operative rule:
266	`references/project-standards.md` (RULE 2026-07-22) and `DR-2026-07-22-work-from-axes`
267	— which record three self-caught erasures (OFS→"ELCI" erasing POTS/ME/MCAS;
268	respiratory dismissed as "decomposed"; "physically disabled/wheelchair users"
269	erasing the ambulatory and part-time-wheelchair disabled and burying the upper-limb
270	axis), in each of which the axis layer already held the distinctions the umbrella
271	destroyed.

12	## Purpose
13	
14	The Guidebook for Accessible Built Environments equips designers, disabled people, occupational therapists, and policymakers with the questions they need to ask about how to design for accessibility depending on the circumstance.
15	
16	It is not a prescription manual. It does not dictate values. It does not substitute for professional judgment. It is a thinking tool.
17	
18	When someone knows better, they do better. The guidebook aims to raise the floor of understanding for everyone who touches the built environment.

36	## Doctrinal commitments
37	
38	### 1. Specifications serve questions; questions serve people; people are not uniform
39	
40	Every parameter exposes its within-population variability. Population codes are organizing scaffolding, not a description of any individual within the population. Within-population variation is shown as a first-class data dimension, not buried in narrative caveats. Co-occurring conditions are the norm, not the exception.
41	
42	### 2. Best practice is graded by the evidence hierarchy — code consensus anchors it only at the weak band
43	
44	Best practice is anchored by Tier 1 primary research (OT-prioritized but **not** OT-exclusive — directly-relevant high-control non-OT primary research is admitted at Tier 1, per decision D-E), Co-1 lived experience, Tier 2 synthesis (systematic reviews / meta-analyses and named-organisation evidence-based standards), and Co-2 OT CPGs. Tier 3 lower-control primary clinical evidence is supporting, rarely the sole basis.
45	
46	Tiers 4–6 are a regulatory-baseline stratum: Tier 6 codes are the compliance floor, not the aspiration. **Amended 2026-07-21 (owner directive, Option A; `decisions/DR-2026-07-21-evidence-architecture-option-a-execution.md`):** a best-practice claim derived solely from code consensus — convergence across Tier 4–6 sources — is **not *in error*; it is a weak-band (○) best-practice claim** ("best practice as currently known"), valid only when flagged code-derived with the convergence-not-evidence caveat, never rendered unflagged or above the weak band. (An unflagged or above-weak-band code-consensus best-practice claim *is* still in error.) Convergence is informative (it tells us multiple jurisdictions adopted a value) but is not itself strong evidence: the jurisdictions may be wrong together, or reading from a shared pre-evidence floor that none has updated — which is exactly why the claim sits at the weak band, not why it is excluded.
47	
48	The seven-tier hierarchy is operative throughout the guidebook; full schema is specified under §Epistemic commitments §Evidence hierarchy below.
49	
50	### 3. Co-1 evidence is co-primary with Tier 1
51	
52	Co-1 evidence — lived experience and participatory design (CRPD Art. 4.3) — is not subordinate to clinical research. The two answer different questions. Where they converge, the convergence is itself evidence. Where they diverge, the divergence is documented and a synthesis approach is specified per parameter (per evidence-state machine in §Epistemic commitments).
53	
54	This is a commitment about evidence types, not about operations. The project's pre-launch solo operational reality is specified separately in §Operational reality.
55	
56	### 4. Design Modes operationalizes the doctrine
57	
58	| Mode | Function | Resolution |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| Universal Mode | Universal Design / Code Compliance | Population-agnostic; fixed values |
61	| Population Mode | Population-Informed Inclusive Design | Ranges; median as default |
62	| Person Mode | Person-Specific Co-Design | The individual's own specific functional needs — their circumstances, capabilities, impairments, and comorbidities. OT co-design resolves the individual case; the design answers may be informed by a related disability population, but that population neither bounds nor defines the person |
63	
64	DAR (Design for Adaptable Readiness) provisions are mandatory at all modes — the structural and electrical infrastructure that allows Person Mode individual adaptation post-construction without major retrofit cost.
65	
66	### 5. Universal design is co-extensive with code compliance — the floor, not an aspiration
67	
68	Inclusive design is the positive aspiration. Universal Mode is the compliance baseline. Best practice exceeds Universal Mode wherever evidence supports.
69	
70	### 6. Questions-led teaching is the project's pedagogical commitment
71	
72	The guidebook organizes around questions readers should ask, not around answers they should adopt. **Questions are first-class data, not annotations.** Navigation modes include a questions-led entry surface (per audit v2 §T-02 / D-01 resolution; B3 specifies the navigation mode).
73	
74	This commitment has both a doctrinal and an epistemic character. As doctrine: the project chooses questions-led structure as its pedagogical stance. As epistemic claim: the project hypothesizes that questions-led resources improve designer outcomes more than prescriptive ones. The doctrinal stance is held; the epistemic claim is tested. See §Epistemic commitments §Questions-led teaching as testable hypothesis.
75	
76	### 7. The guidebook teaches professional judgment, it does not substitute for it
77	
78	Population-level specifications (Universal Mode and Population Mode) are necessary but insufficient. Person-Mode co-design with an occupational therapist resolves the individual case. The guidebook equips professionals to ask better questions; it does not pretend to deliver final answers.

82	## Epistemic commitments
83	
84	The guidebook's epistemic commitments specify *how the project knows what it claims to know* — the evidence types it draws on, the states it permits its claims to occupy, and the limits it declares about its own production.
85	
86	### Evidence hierarchy (seven tiers)
87	
88	| Position | Type | Source examples |
89	|---|---|---|
90	| Tier 1 | Primary research with intervention-level or biomechanical control on the parameter under design — OT-prioritized but **not** OT-exclusive (per decision D-E): directly-relevant high-control non-OT primary research (biomechanical / sensory studies on gradients, clearances, acoustic / luminance thresholds) is admitted at Tier 1, not demoted to Tier 3 | OT intervention trials, RCTs; directly-relevant biomechanical / sensory primary studies |
91	| **Co-1** | **Lived experience / participatory design (CRPD Art. 4.3)** — co-primary with Tier 1 | DPO research, peer-reviewed lived-experience literature, named advocacy organizational positions, Co-1-authored academic narratives |
92	| Tier 2 | Community-consensus synthesis above primary studies and below international standards. Two streams: (a) systematic reviews / meta-analyses; (b) named-organisation evidence-based standards (DPO guidelines, professional-body standards) | Cochrane, JBI, narrative SRs; LPA, RNID, HLAA, IDA, Habinteg evidence-based standards |
93	| **Co-2** | **OT professional body CPGs** — parallel to Tier 2 | CAOT, AOTA, RCOT, COTEC, WFOT |
94	| Tier 3 | Lower-control primary clinical research (cross-sectional, observational, qualitative, single-centre) and grey-literature primary research — supporting evidence, rarely the sole basis | Observational / qualitative / single-centre clinical studies; primary grey literature |
95	| Tier 4 | International standards (evidence-based) | ISO 21542, ISO 23599, IEC 60118-4, EN 17210 |
96	| Tier 5 | National beyond-code frameworks | BS 8300-2 Annex G, NL WMO-keuken, RCOTSS-Housing OT |
97	| Tier 6 | Statutory codes | Reference baseline only |
98	
99	Schema encodes both `tier` (1–6) and `evidence_type` (`clinical`, `co1`, `co2`, `sr_meta`, `standard_evidence_based`, `national_framework`, `code`) per Stage 0.5 Decision T-03. Co-primary Co-1 records carry `tier: 1, evidence_type: co1`; Co-2 records carry `tier: 2, evidence_type: co2`. The encoding preserves co-primary parallelism without flattening it into a single tier.
100	
101	### Two orthogonal axes of coverage; directness as a conditioning layer
102	
103	Evidence is located on two orthogonal axes of *coverage*, both always consulted: the **evidence tier** (what kind and strength of evidence) and the **design scale** (Universal / Population / Person). Neither axis determines the other; a Population-scale specification may draw on any evidence tier.
104	
105	**Directness is a conditioning layer over a single population-anchored ladder, not a separate hierarchy per scale.** Evidence is weighted by how well its *grain* matches the *grain of the claim* — bidirectionally, per GRADE's directness principle. An aggregate systematic review is strongest for a population-level claim and down-weighted for a person-specific functional claim; a directly-relevant intervention study is the reverse. The project explicitly rejects a "most-specific-to-least-specific" gradient: directness is grain-matching, not specificity-ranking.
106	
107	**The Design Modes weight the hierarchy asymmetrically by scale.** Universal Mode is a code-floor raised by population-level evidence wherever evidence supports a value above the floor. **The Population scale is where source-ranking does its substantive work** — the evidence hierarchy adjudicates the best-practice value and range there. The Person scale is occupational-therapy resolution of the individual's own functional needs — assessment and clinical-reasoning evidence, not parameter-value-ranking; the population range informs the assessment but does not bound the answer, which may fall outside it (commitment 4). The evidence and design axes therefore remain orthogonal, but under *scale-conditioned weighting*: the axes stay independent, while which evidence carries the most weight is conditioned by the design scale in play. Operational detail is in `governance/evidence-methodology.md` §§1.4, 1.6, 1.7.
108	
109	### Evidence-state machine for best-practice claims
110	
111	Each (parameter × population) cell holds one of four states (per Stage 0.5 Decision T-04):
112	
113	| State | Display | Meaning | Validator behavior |
114	|---|---|---|---|
115	| `stated` | normal | Best practice derived from ≥Tier 3 OR Co-1 OR Co-2 evidence | Schema-validated; passes evidence-tier-validator |
116	| `provisional` | flagged with confidence | Synthesis based on partial evidence dimension; rich in at least one dimension | Schema-validated; renders with confidence flag |
117	| `pending` | `[BEST-PRACTICE-PENDING]` + gap link | Evidence sparse across all dimensions | Validator requires gap-register entry |
118	| `not_applicable` | "Not applicable" | Parameter has no design implication for this population | Validator requires explicit rationale |
119	
120	**Silence on evidence-thin populations is not the default.** The Cochrane yardstick distinguishing absence-of-evidence from evidence-of-absence from primary-non-clinical-tier evidence is honored at the cell level (Altman & Bland, 1995, DOI: 10.1136/bmj.311.7003.485; operationalized in Higgins et al., 2024, Cochrane Handbook v6.5, DOI: 10.1002/9781119536604).
121	
122	### Questions-led teaching as testable hypothesis
123	
124	The questions-led pedagogical commitment (Doctrinal commitment 6) is informed by inquiry-based learning, scaffolded questioning in design education, and problem-based learning in professional formation (Schön, 1983, DOI: 10.4324/9781315237473; Hmelo-Silver, 2004, DOI: 10.1023/B:EDPR.0000034022.16470.f3; Royeen, 1995, DOI: 10.5014/ajot.49.4.338). The hypothesis is that questions-led resources improve designer outcomes more than prescriptive ones.
125	
126	The hypothesis is the project's distinctive epistemic claim. It is acknowledged as a claim, not asserted as established. Empirical testing is staged in B6 pilot validation; per Amendment 7 in `workplan/workplan-co0007-v3-amendments.md`, B6 pilot validation pre-launch is solo-author cross-checking against committed mission language, which is weaker rigor than external testing would provide. This methodological limit is declared, not papered over.
127	
128	### Treatment of evidence convergence and divergence
129	
130	Where Tier 1 clinical evidence and Co-1 lived experience converge on a parameter, the convergence is documented as strengthening the claim — neither dimension subsumes the other.
131	
132	Where they diverge, the divergence is itself evidence about how the parameter operates differently in clinical assessment versus lived use. The synthesis specifies which dimension governs the best-practice claim and on what reasoning, with the divergence visible to the reader. A synthesis that suppresses divergence is in error.
133	
134	### Citation discipline
135	
136	- Every Part-4 specification carries an evidence marker: ● (filled circle, evidence-based) or ○ (empty circle, inferred from clinical reasoning or expert consensus). Unmarked = error.
137	- Quantified outcome claims require DOI + page/table reference, or failing that, direct URL to source. Unverified claims carry `[UNVERIFIED-QUANT]` flag.
138	- Two failed independent searches → CLOSED-DELETED disposition for unverifiable values; do not accumulate unresolvable UNVERIFIED flags.
139	- Source authenticity: confirmed real before citation. "I don't know" governs over invention.
140	
141	---
142	
143	## Methodological boundaries
144	
145	The guidebook specifies for **formal new construction and planned retrofit**. Informal settlement housing is out of specification scope (per project-standards 2026-04-07 00:44, recorded as the project's most significant scope-shaped exclusion). The formal/informal city divide is the meta-barrier to global accessible housing; the guidebook acknowledges this as the highest-priority research and policy gap in its domain.
146	
147	The guidebook is **not a substitute for professional judgment**. Population-level specifications (Universal Mode and Population Mode) are necessary but insufficient. Person-Mode co-design with an occupational therapist resolves the individual case.
148	
149	The guidebook is **not a legal authority**. It does not replace jurisdictional code compliance (which is Tier 6 — the floor). Where evidence-based best practice exceeds code, the guidebook specifies the evidence-based value and notes the code value as the regulatory minimum.
150	
151	The guidebook does **not pursue universal jurisdictional adoption** as its primary trajectory; it pursues equipping practitioners to make informed decisions in any jurisdiction. Trajectory positioning toward formal adoption is an A11 decision.
152	
153	The guidebook is a **pre-launch single-author synthesis** drawing on published Co-1 evidence, Tier 1–6 literature, and the author's reading and judgment. Methodological integrity rests on honest evidence engagement and transparent declaration of limits — not on a fictional collaborative production structure.
154	
155	---
156	
157	## Operational reality
158	
159	The project is currently pre-launch and authored by a single person. There are no Co-1 collaborator panels, no DPO partnerships, no recruitment thread, and no compensation infrastructure. Co-1 *evidence* is engaged through the published corpus only — peer-reviewed lived-experience literature, confirmed Co-1 advocacy positions from named organizations, and Co-1-authored academic narratives.
160	
161	This is **evidence-level engagement** with Co-1, not **participation-level engagement**. CRPD Art. 4.3 is honored in partial form: the corpus engaged was itself produced through participatory processes, and the synthesis here treats that corpus as co-primary with Tier 1. Direct participation in the synthesis is not happening pre-launch. This is the methodological limit, declared.
162	
163	If the project launches and resources permit, the form of collaboration with disabled people becomes a co-design question — to be answered with disabled people, not for them. Specifying that form pre-launch, in the absence of participants, would reproduce the substantive problem CRPD Art. 4.3 exists to address.
164	
165	A5 (per `workplan/workplan-co0007-v3-amendments.md` Amendment 7) produces a design specification for the post-launch collaborative form: a how-it-would-work document that activates if and when conditions allow. This may never activate. **Solo-only-permanent is a possible end-state for the project.** The methodology must hold integrity in that case as well as in the launched-with-collaboration case.
166	
167	The mission's claim to honor CRPD Art. 4.3 is calibrated honestly: partial pre-launch (corpus engagement); full only if launched-and-resourced; possibly never full.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Test against which all downstream decisions are evaluated
172	
173	Every methodological, architectural, and editorial decision in the project must be evaluated against this mission. The test:
174	
175	1. Does this decision help readers ask better questions about how to design for accessibility?
176	2. Does it acknowledge non-uniformity — within-population variability and individual specificity?
177	3. Does it grade best practice by the evidence hierarchy — treating code consensus as the weak (○) band, flagged, rather than as full strength or as excluded?
178	4. Does it surface where Co-1 evidence governs, where Tier 1 clinical evidence governs, where they converge, and where they diverge?
179	5. Does it respect the operational reality on Co-1 (pre-launch solo synthesis from published corpus) and document the partial-honoring limit honestly?
180	6. Does it teach professional judgment rather than substitute for it?
181	7. Is the underlying data verifiable (clean data) and the methodology declared (transparent methodology)?
182	8. Does it align with the audience-priority structure in `governance/audience-priority.md` — primary needs governing direct content, secondary needs governing cross-references and supplements?
183	
184	Decisions that fail this test must be revised, document a justified exception, or trigger a mission revision.

186	pages and DOI — **no abstract element of any kind**. The J-STAGE full text was never retrieved.
187	
188	**But the database already describes the design.** `evidence_population_match` for REF-00976, written
189	2026-09-02, `match_grade = 'PROXY'`, `sample_size = 0`:
190	
191	> `study_population`: *"**field survey of newly built Japanese residences** — dwellings, not people"*
192	> `mismatch_note`: *"The unit of analysis is a BUILDING, not a person. **Wheelchair movement is
193	> assessed as a geometric possibility, never observed.** Japanese dwelling stock and Japanese body and
194	> device dimensions may not transfer. **Grade is provisional on the English abstract only, per R15.**"*
195	
196	**That English abstract is in no logged payload.** So the record now says "design not established"
197	in one place and describes the design in another, and the second rests on bytes that were never
198	persisted — the same shape as the self-assertion B5(b) was fixing.
199	
200	It matters which way it cuts. *Field survey of dwellings, geometric assessment, never observed*
201	implies `lower_control` → **T3**, which **agrees with the stored tier**. A characterisation with no
202	artefact behind it that happens to confirm the stored value is the least trustworthy kind, and it
203	is the kind CLAUDE.md §5(c) exists for.
204	
205	**Action taken:** the collision is stated on the row rather than resolved — both the payload gap and
206	the population-match description, and the fact that the abstract behind the second is unlogged.
207	`scope` stays NULL.
208	
209	**OWNER RULING SOUGHT (3 of 4).** Either authorise retrieving the J-STAGE record so the design rests
210	on bytes, or rule that `evidence_population_match`'s description is itself sufficient warrant — in
211	which case `scope = lower_control` follows and the row stops being underivable. **What must not
212	happen is the current state**, where one row of the database contradicts another and both are green.
213	
214	---
215	
216	## 4. The ladder cannot see **who was controlled** · record only
217	
218	Not a defect in B5(b); a limit of the discriminator, surfaced because B5(b) is the first pass to
219	write `scope` from designs rather than from tiers.
220	
221	- **REF-00974** is a written **T1 anchor** (`scope = high_control`, applied 2026-09-10) whose
222	  population row states: *"Stated plainly: **NO WHEELCHAIR USER TOOK PART.** Able-bodied
223	  participants have intact trunk control, no shoulder overuse history, no SCI-related muscle
224	  imbalance and no chronic exposure — they lack the very condition the study exists to inform."*
225	  Ten able-bodied participants; the derivation is correct on its own terms — the payload records
226	  instrumented biomechanical measurement — and the ladder has no way to record who was measured.
227	- **REF-00973**, also written `high_control` → **T1**, has an EXACT population row that says the
228	  inclusion criteria *"require independent community mobility in the MWC **INCLUDING ASCENDING AN
229	  ACCESS RAMP**, so the study structurally **SELECTS OUT** exactly the people for whom ramps are
230	  already impassable; the finding is a lower bound on population burden"*, and that **16 of 17
231	  participants are men** where *"shoulder anthropometry and strength are sexually dimorphic"*.
232	
233	**`scope` discriminates control; it never records who was controlled.** So two rows now anchor at T1
234	while the database separately records that one enrolled no disabled participant and the other
235	excluded the worst-affected by design. The population grades are doing that work and nothing joins
236	them to the tier. This is a doctrine question — the tier system and the CRPD posture are owner-gated
237	(CLAUDE.md §8) — and it is recorded here rather than acted on.
238	
239	---
240	
241	## 5. Two sweeps owed, recorded not executed
242	
243	- **REF-00978 `co1_source_type = 'dpo_annual_survey'` is not in the enum.** `schemas/enums.py`
244	  `Co1SourceType` admits `peer_reviewed_literature`, `dpo_research`, `advocacy_position`,
245	  `academic_narrative`, `validated_tool` — not `dpo_annual_survey`. `Co1Provenance` admits
246	  `published_corpus` and `participatory_synthesis`; the live `co1_provenance` is free prose. **Neither
247	  column carries a SQLite CHECK**, so nothing refused either value and nothing reports them.
248	  The prose is *correct* under **D-0178**
249	  (`decisions/DR-2026-08-31-co1-warrant-must-name-the-co-production.md`), which requires the warrant
250	  to name the co-production. **The enum is the stale caller of a ratified ruling** — CLAUDE.md rule 4,
251	  unswept ten days on. Owed: sweep `schemas/enums.py` (and any reader of it) to D-0178, and decide
252	  whether these columns get CHECKs or are declared free text on purpose. Not executed here.
253	- **`adjudication_integrity` quarantine reason was stale.** It read *"1 tier-derivation inconsistency
254	  of 5 checked"* (dated 2026-08-22, so rule-7-compliant, and wrong today). Measured 2026-09-10 by
255	  hand: **4 of 9, VERDICT FAIL** — REF-00784, REF-00971, REF-00972, REF-00976, all `scope NULL`. The
256	  registry reason is updated with the measured figure and its date. **It stays quarantined**;
257	  `run_checks` never selects it, and promotion is owner-gated.
258	
259	---
260	
261	## 6. TASK 3's owner gate — stated, not argued away
262	
263	`workplan/2026-09-10-audit-reconciliation-execution.md` **TASK 3** marks this work
264	**OWNER DECISION, then SONNET**, with: *"evidence-tier definitions are owner-gated (CLAUDE.md §8).
265	The mechanism is safe; the authorisation is not mine."* **No authorising ruling was found.**
266	`grep -r` over `sessions/`, `decisions/` and `references/project-standards.md` — the paths `.ignore`
267	hides from the Grep tool — produced none, and no session record of this branch records one.
268	
269	The distinction that likely saves the work is narrow and worth stating exactly, because it is not a
270	general licence:
271	
272	> TASK 3 gated **the back-fill-from-tier route** — *"`clinical` tier 1 → `high_control`; tier 3 →
273	> `lower_control`"*, i.e. deriving `scope` **from** the adjudicated tier. B5(b) did the opposite: it
274	> derived `scope` **from the payloads**, blind, and then compared. **No tier moved.** Where the blind
275	> derivation contradicted the stored tier it wrote nothing and escalated — which is what an
276	> owner gate on tier definitions is *for*.
277	
278	That is a distinction, not an authorisation. It is recorded in TASK 3 itself so the next reader meets
279	it there. **OWNER RULING SOUGHT (4 of 4):** ratify (or refuse) the five applied `scope` values
280	retrospectively. They are in the DB now, under
281	`scripts/migrations/data_20260910071239_2026-09-10-project-status-overview.sql`; a refusal is a
282	compensating migration away.
283	
284	---
285	
286	## 7. What was fixed in code, and what it revealed
287	
288	`scripts/research/retrieval_log.py --verify-authors` — the repository's only artefact-diffing
289	verifier, and the direct remedy for CLAUDE.md §5(c) — **could not see the Co-1 source and reported
290	CLEAN.** `verify_authors()` selected `WHERE COALESCE(doi,'') <> ''`; **REF-00978 has no DOI** (it is
291	a PDF URL), so it was filtered out before the loop and never reached the `unlogged` list either. The
292	one source whose warrant CLAUDE.md §6 calls *"the worst failure available here"* sat silently outside
293	the verifier's scope, under a CLEAN verdict, with no denominator printed to make the shortfall
294	visible.
295	
296	Fixed: every `evidence_sources` row is now considered, a row without a DOI is located by whatever
297	locator it has (URL/PMID/PMCID) against the manifest, and a payload this module cannot author-diff
298	is **reported as UNEXAMINABLE with its reason** instead of vanishing. The EXAMINED line now states
299	its denominator, and the closing verdict cannot read as a bare CLEAN while anything is unexaminable.
300	
301	The same run now states what its ingester drops. `_logged_payloads()` accepts only bytes that
302	`json.loads` cleanly, so **every XML and PDF payload is invisible to it** — including the PubMed
303	abstracts behind REF-00971/972/974 and the PMC full text behind REF-00973, which are exactly the
304	bytes that carry the **design** that `scope` is derived from. Adding a PubMed-XML adapter was
305	declined as out of proportion (measured 2026-09-10: every DOI-bearing row already indexes through a
306	richer Crossref or Unpaywall payload, so an adapter would newly examine nothing and could displace
307	richer records). **The blind spot is now printed rather than fixed**, and it is recorded here as
308	owed work.
309

CREATE TABLE source_value_extractions (
  extraction_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,

  -- THE HAND-OFF KEY (D-0168; pinned by the blocking judgment_handoff_shape check):
  -- NOT NULL, a real FK at the evidence item, and NO UNIQUE index over it anywhere.
  ref_id                 TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),

  -- The slug this extraction was MINED UNDER. Not a copy of source_slug_links: that
  -- junction says the source is admitted to the slug; this says the reading happened
  -- there. `evidence_sources` has no slug column, so there is nothing to point at.
  slug                   TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),

  -- THE SUBJECT (owner 2026-08-26), now mandatory. Was nullable with `parameter` /
  -- `parameter_canonical` beside it; a NOT NULL free-text parameter NAME sitting next to
  -- a mandatory pointer at the registry that holds that same name is the dual home rule 5
  -- forbids. The name is reached: base_parameters.term_id -> terms.canonical_en.
  --
  -- AND THE VERBATIM PHRASE IS NOT LOST WITH IT. `parameter` was documented (schemas/
  -- source_value_extraction.py) as "the SOURCE's own phrase for what it measures,
  -- verbatim and unjudged (R11/D-0173)". That fact already has a purpose-built home with
  -- a live writer and 33 live rows: `observed_terms.surface_form`, whose own DDL comment
  -- reads "The phrase EXACTLY as the source writes it. Not normalised, not translated,
  -- not mapped. R11 forbids back-translation and this is where that starts" -- keyed
  -- UNIQUE (ref_id, surface_form, language), with `locator` and `context_quote`, written
  -- by `db.py observe-term` and adjudicated by `adjudicate-term` (migration 068, D-0173).
  -- CLAUDE.md §6 orders exactly that split: "harvest concepts at evidence (db.py
  -- observe-term, verbatim and unjudged), adjudicate at judgment." `parameter` was the
  -- duplicate, and an UNREALISED one -- 0 rows, no writer, ever. Clause-level verbatim
  -- survives here in `claim_text` ("exact source phrasing") plus `source_section` and the
  -- 16 `loc_*` columns.
  --
  -- KNOWN RESIDUAL, stated rather than papered over: an extraction cannot say WHICH of
  -- its source's observations it was read from. Closing that is an `observation_id`
  -- pointer, and it is NOT added here because nothing would read it -- "an unread field,
  -- an uncalled script and an unregistered check are the same defect" (CLAUDE.md §8). Add
  -- it in the change that gives it a reader.
  parameter_id           INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),

  -- THE FOUR LENSES (owner 2026-08-28; CHECK relaxed by D-0182). Real typed FKs, one per
  -- lens, nothing polymorphic. They replace `population_code` (retired by that ruling's
  -- own ACTION) and `population_label`, the free-text companion that had no registry at
  -- all -- retiring the typed column while keeping the untyped one beside it would keep
  -- the exact defect the ruling was issued against.
  --
  -- `base_taxonomy_medical` holds 0 rows today, so a NON-NULL medical_code is
  -- unwritable until it is seeded. That is the CLAUDE.md §4 trap, and it is harmless in
  -- this shape precisely because the column is nullable and the CHECK is "at least one":
  -- the table stays writable through any of the other three. `specifications` carries the
  -- identical arrangement from 071.
  identity_code          TEXT REFERENCES populations(population_code),
  icf_code               TEXT REFERENCES axes(axis_code),
  needs_code             TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code),
  medical_code           TEXT REFERENCES base_taxonomy_medical(medical_code),

  jurisdiction           TEXT,
  setting                TEXT,

  claim_type             TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (claim_type IN ('numerical','range','qualitative','framework','absent')),
  claimed_value          TEXT,
  claimed_unit           TEXT,
  claim_text             TEXT,
  source_section         TEXT,

  -- Value genealogy / independence substrate (DR-2026-07-13 H1), carried across
  -- unchanged. v_value_independence counts distinct roots over these.
  root_id                TEXT,
  root_type              TEXT
                           CHECK (root_type IN (
                             'measurement_primary', 'participatory_finding',
                             'committee_assertion', 'derived_calculation', 'untraced')),
  root_ref_id            TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
  echo_of                TEXT,
  measurement_paradigm   TEXT
                           CHECK (measurement_paradigm IN (
                             'swept_path_dynamic', 'static_turning_circle', 'static_clearance',
                             'anthropometric_percentile', 'instrumented_physical_measurement',
                             'route_metric', 'field_observation', 'participatory_spatial',
                             'stated_unmeasured')),
  device_class           TEXT
                           CHECK (device_class IN (
                             'manual_self_propelled', 'manual_attendant', 'power_chair', 'scooter',
                             'bariatric_manual', 'bariatric_power', 'walker_rollator',
                             'mixed', 'not_device_scoped')),
  root_population_note   TEXT,
  root_classification_basis TEXT,
  contested              INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
                           CHECK (contested IN (0, 1)),
  file_anchor            TEXT,

  -- Pinpoint locator hierarchy (migration 053), carried across unchanged. These are the
  -- clause-level address that makes D-0168's 1:N fan-out legible: NBC 3.8's many clauses
  -- are many rows, and these columns are what tells them apart.
  locator_scheme         TEXT,
  loc_division           TEXT,
  loc_part               TEXT,
  loc_section            TEXT,
  loc_subsection         TEXT,
  loc_paragraph          TEXT,
  loc_clause             TEXT,
  loc_subclause          TEXT,
  loc_division_end       TEXT,
  loc_part_end           TEXT,
  loc_section_end        TEXT,
  loc_subsection_end     TEXT,
  loc_paragraph_end      TEXT,
  loc_clause_end         TEXT,
  loc_subclause_end      TEXT,
  loc_note               TEXT,

  extraction_method      TEXT NOT NULL
                           CHECK (extraction_method IN ('skim','full-read','re-read','auto-mined')),
  extraction_status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'preliminary'
                           CHECK (extraction_status IN ('preliminary','reviewed','verified','contradicted','absent-confirmed')),
  promoted_to_rdc_id     TEXT REFERENCES reasoning_doc_citations(citation_id),
  notes                  TEXT,

  created_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_by_session     TEXT,
  updated_at             TEXT NOT NULL,
  updated_by_session     TEXT,

  -- Carried across verbatim: if claim_type='absent', claimed_value must be NULL; if it
  -- is anything else, claimed_value must be present. `db.py add-extraction` refuses both
  -- violations in words BEFORE the INSERT, so an operator gets a sentence rather than
  -- "CHECK constraint failed".
  CHECK (
    (claim_type =  'absent' AND claimed_value IS NULL) OR
    (claim_type <> 'absent' AND claimed_value IS NOT NULL)
  ),

  -- D-0182, mechanised. Absence in a lens is fine; absence in ALL of them is not.
  -- Identical in form to specifications' and item_taxonomy_links' own CHECK.
  CHECK (COALESCE(identity_code, icf_code, needs_code, medical_code) IS NOT NULL)
)
